title: Price accepts Infinity, exponent forms and sub-cent values; line amounts and total disagree
evidence: Number() is used as the validator (app.js:18) and the only check is `price > 0` (app.js:19). Number('Infinity') is Infinity, which passes; Number('1e3') is 1000; '0.004' passes. Line prices are displayed with toFixed(2) (app.js:8) but the total sums the unrounded products (app.js:10). Money is held as float.
failing_case: Enter qty 1, price 'Infinity': the line renders 'Infinity' and Total shows 'Infinity'; the POST body JSON.stringify turns Infinity into null, so the server receives price null. Separately, three lines at price 1.004 each render '1 × 1.00' (sum 3.00) while Total shows 3.01, so the visible lines do not add up to the invoice total.
remediation: Parse price with one validator: finite, matches /^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$/, and store integer minor units; compute line and total from the integers in one pure, tested function.

title: Invalid line input is dropped silently: no error message, no focus, nothing says why
evidence: app.js:19 returns with no feedback for any invalid quantity or price. index.html has no error region and no aria-invalid / aria-describedby. Only client has the native `required` attribute (index.html:14); qty and price do not.
failing_case: User types quantity '2.5' or price '1,50' (comma decimal, common in many locales; Number('1,50') is NaN) and presses 'Add line'. Nothing happens: no message, no highlight, the values stay. The user cannot tell what is wrong. This fails WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification (level A) and 3.3.3.
remediation: On failure, set aria-invalid on the offending field, write a specific message ('Quantity must be a whole number of 1 or more') into an element linked by aria-describedby, announce it, and move focus to the first bad field. Consider accepting a comma decimal.

quote: const res = await fetch("/api/invoices", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(lines) });
title: Send and Void do not handle a rejected fetch; a network failure is silent
evidence: app.js:26 and app.js:33 await fetch with no try/catch. Only a non-2xx response (res.ok) is handled at app.js:27 and :34. A rejected promise (offline, DNS, CORS, abort) skips both alerts and becomes an unhandled rejection in the console.
failing_case: User goes offline (or the server is down at the TCP level) and clicks 'Send invoice'. fetch rejects with TypeError. No alert, no message, no state change. The user cannot tell whether the invoice went out and may re-send or assume it was sent. The same applies to 'Void invoice'.
remediation: Wrap both calls in try/catch, show the cause and a next step ('No connection. The invoice was not sent. Check your network and try again.') in a status region, and leave the form state unchanged.

title: Void invoice button is visible and silently does nothing for a non-admin, which is the shipped user
evidence: The signed-in user is { roles: ["viewer", "billing"] } (app.js:2), so canVoid is false and the handler returns at app.js:32 with no message. The button (index.html:24) is always enabled and looks like Send. On a successful void, app.js:34 also shows nothing.
failing_case: Sam clicks 'Void invoice'. Nothing visible happens, no request is sent, no message. Sam cannot tell whether the invoice was voided or the click was refused.
remediation: Hide or disable the button (with a visible reason) when the user cannot void, and show a message on refusal and on success.

title: Double-send guard is a 1-second timer, not an in-flight guard; a slow request can be sent twice
evidence: guards.js:21-26 only compares Date.now() to the previous click. app.js:25-26 has no in-flight flag, no disabled button, no idempotency key. The lines array is not cleared after a successful send (app.js:28), so a second POST carries the same content.
failing_case: On a 3 s response, the user clicks Send at t=0, sees nothing happen (no feedback, see the other finding), and clicks again at t=1.5 s. tooSoon() returns false, a second POST /api/invoices is issued with the same lines. The client is invoiced twice. Even after success, clicking again after 1 s resends the same invoice.
remediation: Disable the button (or hold an in-flight flag) from click until the response settles, send an idempotency key with the POST, and drop the time-based guard.

title: Whitespace-only client passes `required` and is pushed as an empty name
evidence: Native `required` (index.html:14) accepts ' '. app.js:16 trims it to '' and nothing checks client afterwards (app.js:19-20). render() then emits `` (app.js:8).
failing_case: Type three spaces in Client, qty 1, price 5, press Add line. A line with an empty client is added and sent to the server; the list item shows an empty link with no accessible name and ': 1 × 5.00'.
remediation: Validate client after trim (non-empty) alongside the quantity and price checks, and show the error next to the field.

title: Send posts an empty invoice when no lines have been added
evidence: The handler (app.js:24-29) calls tooSoon() then fetch with JSON.stringify(lines) and never checks lines.length. lines starts as [] (app.js:1). Initial state in index.html shows Total 0.00 with an enabled Send button.
failing_case: Fresh page load, click 'Send invoice'. POST /api/invoices with body "[]" is sent. Depending on the server this creates an empty invoice or returns an error that the user sees only as 'The invoice was not sent. Try again.' with no cause.
remediation: Disable Send until lines.length > 0, and guard in the handler as well; say 'Add at least one line before sending'.

title: Successful send shows nothing: sentCount is never displayed and the list is not cleared
evidence: sentCount is written at app.js:28 and read nowhere (grep). On success there is no message, no disabled state, and render() is not called. The Send button has no pending state while the request runs.
failing_case: User clicks 'Send invoice' on a working server. The page looks exactly as before. They cannot distinguish success from a dead button, so they click again (see the double-send finding) or leave unsure.
remediation: Show a status line in an aria-live region ('Invoice sent') on success, show 'Sending...' with the button disabled during the request, and clear or lock the lines afterwards. Remove sentCount if nothing uses it.

title: Void permission is enforced only in the browser, from a user object the page itself defines
evidence: app.js:2 defines `const user = { ... roles: [...] }` in the page; app.js:32 gates the request with canVoid(user). The void POST (app.js:33) carries no credentials or data of its own, and no server code is in the payload to show it re-checks the role.
failing_case: Open the console and run user.roles.push('admin') (a top-level const binding is reachable from the console, and the array is mutable), then click 'Void invoice': the POST /api/invoices/void is sent. If the server trusts the request, a billing-only user voids an invoice. q: does the server check the role? Not visible here.
remediation: Enforce the admin role on the server from the session; the client may hide or disable the button, but must never be the gate. Load the user from the server rather than hard-coding it.

title: Live region is re-rendered wholesale with innerHTML, so every added line re-announces the whole list
evidence: render() (app.js:7) replaces the entire contents of the live <ul> on every add. Screen readers treat the replaced nodes as new content. No aria-atomic or additions-only handling.
failing_case: With 10 lines in the list, adding the 11th makes a screen reader read out all 11 items again, and the Total, instead of the one new line.
remediation: Append only the new <li> instead of replacing innerHTML, or move the announcement to a separate status element ('Line added: Acme, 2 × 5.00. Total 10.00').

title: Destructive Void action has no confirmation, no undo and the same styling as the primary Send action
evidence: index.html:23-24 place two identical, adjacent buttons; styles.css:4 gives all buttons the same style. app.js:31-35 posts straight away with no confirmation and no invoice id in the request.
failing_case: An admin who mis-clicks the adjacent 'Void invoice' instead of 'Send invoice' voids with no prompt. The request names no invoice, so the user also cannot tell which invoice was voided.
remediation: Make Send the one primary button, style Void as a secondary or danger action placed apart, ask for confirmation naming the invoice ('Void invoice INV-123? This cannot be undone.'), and send the invoice id.

title: Each client name is a focusable link to '#' that does nothing useful
evidence: app.js:8 wraps every client in <a href="#"> with no handler; title repeats the link text.
failing_case: Keyboard user tabs through one stop per line; Enter jumps the page to the top and adds '#' to the URL. The link promises navigation it does not deliver.
remediation: Render the client name as plain text, or link to a real client page and drop the redundant title.
